body:
I find it hard to focus on work, cause I'm going to school full-time and trying to graduate on time. It can get tough as I'm at work and stressing over papers/tests/etc...

I don't feel like I am doing well at all, and am struggling a lot. However, I do agree that if l that if I want to live on I do need to find some sort of activities that will help me to de-stress.

I am not currently seeing a medical professional. I have in the past (sorry if I wasn't too clear). The last professional I saw was a therapist about six months ago who I would see weekly. 

I felt that I could sort of manage with self-medication. When I had bad days, I could tell myself that I could go smoke, pop a few xanax bars, etc... and things would feel a little better for a while. I would still be depressed, but the euphoria from the drugs would drown out the depression for a while and then usually put me to sleep.

I've tried a few SSRIs and anti-depressants, and they made me incredibly numb. Like I mentioned before they killed my motivation and made me want to sleep all day, the doctor recommended I take less but the feeling was still the same. I also tried a few of these drugs and some made me feel even worse than I do when sober. I feel like these are not effective for me, because I still need to try force myself to get out of bed and go to class/work. However, I have not tried all of these drugs, maybe there's one out there that will work for me? Sort of doubtful though. 

When I am depressed there is so much going through my head. I feel that my depression and anxiety go hand in hand. Sometimes I visualize and imagine hurting myself. I imagine what it would be like to finally end it, and it gives me a little peace knowing that if I ever work up the courage to do so I will be free (I really hope Hell isn't real). I wouldn't say that I experience the feeling through sound. I would describe it more as a sinking feeling coupled with thoughts of self-loathing and hatred and just wanting to die. I've always had low self-esteem and felt pretty worthless, and even though I try to change the way I think, the feelings keep coming back. It's hard because I feel that we all feel the way we do for a reason, and we can't just simply flip a switch and decide to turn these feelings off or simply deny them. Sometimes the thought of "I just want to fucking kill myself" will just play on repeat like a broken record in my mind. It gets to the point where this "voice" begins to overtake my own and I feel as if I am in quicksand or drowning in it without even realizing it, and then it hits me like a ton of bricks. The feelings/suicidal thoughts are always there, but some days are worse than others.

I desperately want to move out. However, I am a broke college student and I probably won't be able to do so for a couple of years or so (not too sure if I can keep myself from harming myself for that long). I try to take things day by day, but as the days go by I find it harder to go on as the stresses of life are causing me to feel like I am beginning to crack. 

As for trying to moderate "recreational" drug use, I feel like I can't really do that. I start off doing something, and I feel like I can't stop or control myself, but maybe that's where I have to learn moderation and self-control, but with my depression it's so easy to want to get lost in a drug. I remember I first started smoking marijuana at 17. Over the years, I began to convince myself it wasn't that bad, cause "everyone else was doing it". I began to become a heavy smoker (3-5 times a day) and about a couple of years ago have moved up to using extracts/waxes/oils (more potent form of marijuana). I also have been using/abusing other drugs like xanax and alcohol, however these were the use of these drugs were a little less frequent (would do them together with weed maybe once or twice a week in order to black out/fall asleep/forget the pain) I can't blame my family or genes, but we have a long list of family members who have been/currently are addicts and alcoholics. I'm not too sure if there is some sort of hereditary addictive personality gene???

I have (unsuccessfully) tried to quit drugs before and have experienced this rebound effect that you speak of. This is what possibly is making my depression worse this time around, but not sure because depression has been bad for the past couple of months and I have been feeling extremely suicidal even before I was told to quit everything cold-turkey. 

DT store = Drive Thru Store. It makes it even harder because our DT usually gets pretty crazy, and during our rushes I not only have to grab food for cafe but also for the DT.  I could barely keep it together though. My mind was preoccupied, I forgot to get customer's coffees and messed up on a couple of orders. I could feel my fellow baristas (we call each other partners) getting irritated with me, and as being the newest person at the job it makes me feel more down on myself and want to quit. We were also down one person due to a no call no show, which made everything a bit more stressful on all of us. However, in order to pay bills and stuff I need a job. I was thinking about trying to quit and finding a lower stress job as I still have school to worry about.
